note: Literature directly reports two distinct patterns of isolated CLN3 retinal disease: an early-onset severe form with macular atrophy (~60%) and a milder middle/late-onset form with foveal preservation (~40%).

evidence.text: In a cohort of 15 patients with isolated nonsyndromic IRD caused by biallelic CLN3 variants, two distinct patterns were observed: severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes in 9 patients (60%) and mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset in 6 patients (40%).

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: Two distinct patterns of retinal disease could be identified: a mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset (n = 6; legal blindness threshold reached by 70s) and a severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes (n = 9; legal blindness threshold reached by 40s).

evidence.text: Among 10 patients with isolated CLN3-associated retinal degeneration, 6 presented with early-onset disease (mean age 12.1 years) and severe photoreceptor loss, while 4 presented with late-onset rod-cone dystrophy (mean age 29.7 years) and focal preservation of the ellipsoid zone and outer nuclear layer in the fovea.

source.title: Detailed Clinical Phenotype and Molecular Genetic Findings in CLN3-Associated Isolated Retinal Degeneration
source.quote: Of the 10 patients, 4 had a progressive late-onset rod-cone dystrophy, with a mean (range) age at onset of 29.7 (20-40) years, and 6 had an earlier onset rod-cone dystrophy, with a mean (range) age at onset of 12.1 (7-17) years.
